calls.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
calls.text: {"summary": "Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that allows large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources. This process supplements the LLM's pre-existing training data, enabling them to use domain-specific or updated information. RAG improves LLM performance by blending the LLM process with information retrieval to help LLMs stick to facts and reduce AI hallucinations.", "details": [{"text": "Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "With RAG, LLMs first refer to a specified set of documents, then respond to user queries.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "These documents supplement information from the LLM's pre-existing training data.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "RAG improves LLMs by incorporating information retrieval before generating responses.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "RAG pulls relevant text from databases, uploaded documents, or web sources.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "RAG reduces the need to retrain LLMs with new data, saving on computational and financial costs.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "RAG allows LLMs to include sources in their responses, so users can verify the cited sources.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "The term retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) was introduced in a 2020 paper that described combining a parametric language model with a non-parametric external memory accessed through retrieval at inference time.", "section": "S1"}]}
